_comment: Field-alias table for ${Provider/field} reference resolution, asserted from
This fixture exists because the two had already drifted: PASSWORD, PASS and
PWD were present in TypeScript and absent in Rust, so ${PgProd/password}
resolved in the desktop app and reached .pgpass, envv render, envv exec and
every CLI export as the literal text ${PgProd/password}. A broken deploy
whose error message names nothing useful.
Keys are the alias as written in a reference; values are the vault-entry
JSON field the reference must resolve to. Each side builds an entry whose
every field holds its own name, resolves ${E/<alias>}, and asserts it got
the expected field back — so this tests the real resolution path rather
_unresolvable_comment: Phase 21. `ID` used to fall through to `_ => field` in canonical_field, so
entry_field looked up `entry.id` — the row's UUID — found it non-empty and
returned it. The CLI therefore wrote a vault UUID into a rendered config
while the app, whose switch had no `id` case, left ${Spotify/ID} as literal
text. One reference, two wrong answers, neither reported.
These field names must resolve to nothing on both sides. The entry the
harness builds carries all four with non-empty values, so removing the
deny-list makes these cases fail rather than pass by absence.
_extra_var_fallback_comment: A client id lives in extra_vars in every vault written before Phase 22's
value roles exist. Both sides fall through from an empty built-in field to
extra_vars, so ${F/ID} resolves there — and both must, or the alias arm
above is useful in the CLI only.
